prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1262; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a collision at an intersection where the insured vehicle was turning left and was struck in the side by another vehicle. The claimant reports a shoulder injury and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage period.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact. Responding officers also noted the claimant's presence in the vehicle when they arrived.

Entry 4: Reviewed the photographs taken at the scene. They confirm several details of the account, including the position of the vehicles after impact.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle damage. The pattern and location of the damage match the impact described by the claimant.

Entry 6: Checked prior claim history on the vehicle and found no earlier damage to the same areas.

Entry 7: Interviewed the claimant, who described the collision consistently with the first statement. The claimant added a few minor details about the traffic signal and speed, but the core account has not changed.

Entry 8: Searched for independent witnesses. None were identified, so the account rests on the photographs, the physical damage, and the police findings.

Entry 9: Reviewed the medical records. The shoulder injury is consistent in type and severity with the force of a side impact of this kind.

Entry 10: Noted that the claimant had a minor shoulder strain several years ago in the same area, which healed completely with no lasting limitation. The current treatment has been assessed separately from that earlier episode.

Entry 11: Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits. Symptoms and treatment frequency have tapered as the claimant has improved.

Entry 12: Current status: liability and damage are supported by the file, and the injury claim is being evaluated against the treatment records and recovery progress. Reserve reviewed; file to remain open pending final medical update.
